name: GIFFORDS
subject: Project 2025 could roll back all of our progress
disclaimer_text: Paid For By Giffords PAC; not authorized by any candidate or candidate's committee
body:
The Project 2025 agenda would defund federal law enforcement, while making it easier for anyone to have access to a gun.
#

Friend -
By now, you’ve most likely heard of Project 2025—the 900-page long policy agenda written by the Heritage Foundation, an ultra-conservative think tank.
At its core, Project 2025 threatens our democracy and gives Donald Trump the power to weaponize our government to enact his extreme MAGA policies. Project 2025 has the potential to roll back all of the progress we’ve made in our movement for gun safety.
If Donald Trump were to take back the White House, we can be sure that he will begin to carry out this playbook on day one of his presidency. After all, it was written by veterans of his administration.
[**Will you fuel our work to protect our gun safety movement from the dangerous proposals in Project 2025 by contributing $3 to GIFFORDS PAC today?**](https://go.giffords.org/go/14457?c0=giffords-em-july24.-nTEO4&refcode=em240725-2-30&t=1&akid=8578%2E3935704%2EAsZW9F)
**The Project 2025 agenda would make it far easier for anyone to have access to a gun—no questions asked.**
A concerning policy proposal that has already been released in a recent Republican Study Committee Budget is the Concealed Carry Reciprocity Act. Although 21 states and the District of Columbia do not allow people to permitless carry, the Concealed Carry Reciprocity Act would overrule state laws on carrying concealed guns. We are on the cusp of electing the first Black woman to serve as President of the United States. Sometimes it’s hard for me to wrap my head around how much progress we’ve made in just a couple of generations. **Peter, I grew up during segregation in North Carolina – a future in Congress only existed in my wildest dreams.** Community engagement has always been a cornerstone of my life, but due to systemic barriers growing up, pursuing a career in politics didn’t feel attainable. **Now it’s 2024, I’m representing NC-04 in Congress, and we have the opportunity to elect the first Black woman as president in November.** Kamala Harris’ presidential campaign is not only inspiring, but it is groundbreaking. Friend, it's Senate Majority Leader Chuck Schumer, and I'm reaching out because Colin Allred is officially the Democratic nominee to run against and defeat Ted Cruz, and I need you to donate $20 to help him and Serve America win. [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/serve-allred]
Let me tell you why your support is so important. The race to defeat Ted Cruz doesn't just concern Texans – it concerns the future of our democracy.
Our country can't handle six more years of Ted Cruz, his attacks on reproductive freedoms, his dismantling of our fundamental voting rights, and his endless self-centered antics. He's proven time and time again that his only loyalty is to himself, not the people he's supposed to represent.
It's time to send him packing. Not only because Texans deserve so much better – but because if Colin wins, Democrats are virtually guaranteed to retain control of the Senate, which is our last line of defense against the far right.
Colin can win this – Cruz won by just 2.6% of the vote in 2018. Election experts know it, and recent polling numbers show them TIED. But he'll need a massive movement of grassroots supporters behind him to help him reach voters, pull ahead, and win.
That starts today with you, friend. Colin needs to raise $65,000 by midnight tonight so that he can stay on track to reach enough voters and win in November. That's why I'm personally asking: Will you donate $20 right now to power Colin and Serve America to victory and defeat Ted Cruz? With your help, we can finally give Texans the leadership they deserve and protect the future of our democracy. [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/serve-allred]
Thank you,
Chuck Schumer

1 year after my thirst strike, we have federal protections
Peter,
One year ago today, I stood on the steps of the Capitol in the summer heat for nine hours without water. Why?
**I held an all-day thirst strike in solidarity with workers in Texas and across the nation who lacked federal heat safety protections. And one year later, President Biden announced the first-ever federal rule to protect tens of millions of workers from extreme heat.**
With the support of workers from across the nation, we called on the federal government to guarantee basic protections like water breaks for workers—which Greg Abbott eliminated on behalf of his billionaire donors.** **
But when we organize, we win.
For so many working families across our country, these safety protections are a matter of life and death. That’s why it’s so important that we organize, community-by-community, industry-by-industry, to push back against politicians fighting for profits instead of people.
I’ll keep fighting for workers in Texas and across the country every day in Congress. clean_body: 1 year after my thirst strike, we have federal protections Peter, One year ago today, I stood on the steps of the Capitol in the summer heat for nine hours without water. Why? I held an all-day thirst strike in solidarity with workers in Texas and across the nation who lacked federal heat safety protections. And one year later, President Biden announced the first-ever federal rule to protect tens of millions of workers from extreme heat. With the support of workers from across the nation, we called on the federal government to guarantee basic protections like water breaks for workers—which Greg Abbott eliminated on behalf of his billionaire donors. But when we organize, we win. For so many working families across our country, these safety protections are a matter of life and death. That’s why it’s so important that we organize, community-by-community, industry-by-industry, to push back against politicians fighting for profits instead of people. I’ll keep fighting for workers in Texas and across the country every day in Congress. But I can’t do it without your support.= = Tom Williams/Getty Images **= Together, we can keep delivering results for workers and their families in the years ahead. Thank you for being on this team. In Solidarity, -Greg Greg Casar Congressman Texas Congressional District 35 ****=** | ****** ---|---

The work we do in this first week will determine our success come November.
# [](https://act.katieporter.com/go/9?t=1&akid=39001%2E3422442%2EgwQKef)
Derek, I’ve known Vice President Harris for more than a decade—since 2012.
[](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ttp-em-20240725?refcode=em20240725-39001&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&refcode2=39001_3422442_gwQKef&akid=39001%2E3422442%2EgwQKef)
When she was Attorney General of California, Kamala appointed me to be California's independent watchdog over the Big Banks during the housing foreclosure crisis.
I have seen firsthand how Kamala fearlessly stands up for working people. Kamala understands that the real victory is making a difference in people's lives, not just securing wins on paper. That’s why I was honored when Kamala appointed me to enforce the foreclosure settlement and hold the Big Banks’ feet to the fire to help homeowners.
Kamala endorsed me on the first day of my campaign when I ran for Congress in 2018. I have been so grateful for her support over the many years. Now, I’m proud to strongly support her candidacy for President.
We must do everything we can to elect Democrats up and down the ballot who share our values. I have seen Kamala’s values firsthand and I know she will stand up for working families. Kamala is fearless, and she’s ready to lead as President. **I wholeheartedly endorse her to be our Democratic nominee.**
The work we do this first week will determine our success come November. The press and pundits want to gauge whether or not she has momentum out the gate.

Vice President Kamala Devi Harris was born in Oakland, California, on October 20, 1964. Harris is the daughter of immigrants. Her father is a Jamaican economics professor and her mother was a scientist working on breast cancer, who came to the United States from India at the age of 19 and then received her doctorate the same year that Kamala was born. Her whole career path from law to politics has been defined by many firsts. She was the first Indian American senator and California’s first female and** ** South Asian attorney general. clean_body: | | | Hi Friend, Welcome to the latest New Pennsylvania Project newsletter! In this edition, you'll find critical election news, upcoming events, and exciting career opportunities. We’re here to keep you informed about our progress to eliminate voting barriers. We will continue to provide key election updates, and highlight the issues that shape Pennsylvania's future. As we gear up for the 2024 general election, we invite you to join us in our mission to mobilize voters to the polls in every election, and to make change in our communities. #WhenWeVoteWeWin | | | | | | | | GETTY Vice President Kamala Devi Harris was born in Oakland, California, on October 20, 1964. Harris is the daughter of immigrants. Her father is a Jamaican economics professor and her mother was a scientist working on breast cancer, who came to the United States from India at the age of 19 and then received her doctorate the same year that Kamala was born. Her whole career path from law to politics has been defined by many firsts. She was the first Indian American senator and California’s first female and South Asian attorney general. Speaking of her mother ten years after her passing, Harris said: "My mother would look at me and she’d say, ‘Kamala, you may be the first to do many things, but make sure you are not the last.'"- On January 20, 2021, Kamala Harris was sworn in as Vice President of the United States – the first woman, the first Black American, and the first South Asian American to be elected to this position. Now, as to position her as the Democratic Party’s 2024 presidential nominee, Harris could be on the cusp of becoming the country’s first female president. "Now that President Joe Biden has dropped out of the presidential race and endorsed Harris, it seems likely she will be the new nominee. Here’s her record on voting rights in the Biden administration and in her career as a senator." “For the first time in at least 16 years, the Democratic and Republican parties in Pennsylvania are within half a million registered voters of one another...The number of people registered as independents or under a third party has also grown, from 11% of total registered voters in 2008 to 15% this year.” "A flurry of recent bipartisan agreements by state lawmakers on energy projects and policies is sending a clear message: Pennsylvania is slowly moving toward clean energy but fossil fuels aren’t going anywhere." “Whether Gov. Josh Shapiro wins the veepstakes or not, Democratic lawmakers and officials expressed confidence that Pennsylvania will deliver a victory in the Nov. 5 presidential election for their party’s standard bearer Kamala Harris.” “If Shapiro is chosen as Kamala Harris' running mate and they win the presidential election, Davis would take over as Pennsylvania's governor...Davis is prepared to take over whenever he may be asked, he said at a news conference Wednesday in Lancaster.” “As Ms. Harris turns her attention to selecting a running mate, the interviews show no clear consensus among this group of party insiders over whom she should pick: 16 percent of respondents said it should be Josh Shapiro, the governor of Pennsylvania, and 11 percent said Mark Kelly, the senator from Arizona. About 28 percent of respondents said they did not know whom the selection should be, or they did not respond to the question.” “The campaign said earlier it took in $81 million in the 24 hours after Mr. Biden dropped out. It was the largest amount of money raised in a 24-hour span in presidential history, according to Team Harris...The $100 million haul came from more than 1.1 million unique donors, including 62% first-time donors.” “In Pennsylvania, should the Democrats retain the White House in November and Shapiro moves onto Washington, Lt. Gov. Austin Davis would assume the governor’s role, while Senate President Pro Tempore Kim Ward (R-Westmoreland) will take over as Lieutenant Governor and become President of the Senate.” "Pennsylvania’s highest court will weigh in on the legality of Pittsburgh’s tax on out-of-town athletes and performers. In an order issued Monday, the state Supreme Court said it would hear arguments about whether lower courts misinterpreted a constitutional requirement that taxes be levied uniformly." . | | | Breaking barriers: Pennsylvanians share why Kamala Harris’ presidential bid gives them hope “Besides the representation part, which is important, in my case... my daughter was conceived by IVF and so basically it concerns me that this choice could be taken away or even eliminated.” -Dyneco Gibson Read in how New Pennsylvania Project's board members, Senator Patty Kim, and Speaker of the House, Joanna McClinton, along with NPP's director of campaigns & engagement, Dyneco Gibson, and our CEO, Kadida Kenner, are finding inspiration in Vice President Kamala Harris’ run for the White House. CEO Kadida Kenner as guest speaker on Areva Martin in Real Time "We are experiencing a climate in which women of all races, all creeds, are standing up for themselves and what is best for them." Watch Kadida Kenner talk about what is at stake during this election during her interview with Areva Martin on KBLA 1580. | | | | | | | | | UNITED AGAINST PROJECT 2025 / AGENDA 47 RALLY Saturday, July 27th, 2024 at 6:30 pmChester County Historic Courthouse 3 N High St, West Chester, PA 19380 New Pennsylvania Project's CEO, Kadida Kenner, will be there to help open up the event. We need to do everything in our power to keep Project 2025 and now Agenda 47 from happening. | Join us in the City of Chester for a Block Party to celebrate our Headquarters Grand Opening! The New Pennsylvania Project has a new headquarters in the City of Chester. Save the date for the celebration on Tuesday, August 13th, from 5:30-8:00 pm at 2619 9th Street, Chester, PA. This is a family-friendly event with FREE food, sweet treats, activities for the kids, and of course, the opportunity to get registered to vote or check your voter's status. We will also have a screening of the documentary: "Suppressed and Sabotaged." For more information email us at: info@newpaproject.org | | | | | NPP ON THE GROUND New Philly regional organizing director, Marcus, engaging a voter at her door. | Connie talks to a man on his way to the bus. Connie registering a voter on her stoop. | | The Philly team is now on the ground, as we moved into our office at 29th & Cecil B. Moore earlier this week. The team walked the surrounding blocks, introduced themselves to the neighborhood, and registered Philadelphians to vote!There’s a special election for the vacated state representative seats in the 195th and 201st districts. The election will take place on September 17th.Starting Monday, July 29th, the Philly NPP office will be open daily. Stop by if you need registered to vote or need to check your voter status! | | | “Regarding the provisional ballots, Walsh is contesting a Commonwealth Court decision that granted Cabell’s request to count a Butler Township ballot cast by Cabell’s cousin, Shane O’Donnell, and reject a ballot cast by Lake Township voter Timothy J. Wagner. Walsh is seeking the opposite: rejection of O’Donnell’s ballot and acceptance of Wagner’s ballot.”** "In a long-shot effort, Rep. Susan Wild launched a discharge petition in hopes of forcing the House to vote on a bill to codify the right to in vitro fertilization services nationwide." “Concerns that judges on the nation’s highest courts have not properly disclosed personal conflicts — and have failed to recuse when such issues arose — have been at the center of a recent national debate. | Peter,

Granite Staters deserve a leader who will fight for the values that bring us together by prioritizing people over politics, collaboration over conflict, and bringing our community together to solve the challenges we face.

At a time when politics seems more divided than ever, Maggie understands that by working together, we can address the issues that matter most and help support our families, our economy, and our future.

Electing our slate of climate champions will supercharge our climate fight in Pennsylvania and send a powerful message nationwide.

**1\. Hadley Haas, HD-44:** Hadley understands the threat the climate crisis poses to her home district and the planet. As a fierce protector of clean air and clean water, she will fight for healthy, resilient communities in the State House. **2\. Danielle Friel Otten, HD-155:** Danielle knows what it takes to lead in a community directly impacted by the fossil fuel industry. As an organizer, she opposed the Mariner East Pipeline, a fracked gas project running through her neighborhood. And as an elected official, she has championed legislation on pipeline safety, renewable energy, and accountability for Big Oil. **3\. Megan Kocher, HD-119:** Megan understands the urgency of the climate crisis, not only for our planet, but for the health and well-being of communities across the state. She is committed to decreasing Pennsylvania’s dependence on fossil fuels and investing in new high-paying jobs needed to support the transition to a clean energy future. **4\. Nikil Saval, SD-1:** Nikil has a proven record of fighting for our planet and for the people of Pennsylvania. In his time in office, Nikil has sponsored and passed legislation to encourage energy efficiency in the housing sector and minimize fossil fuel reliance — especially in Pennsylvania’s schools. **5\. Andre Carroll, HD-201:** Andre is deeply committed to ensuring that Pennsylvanians’ rights to clean air and water are respected and protected. If elected, Andre will represent the Germantown section of Philadelphia and is aware of Big Oil’s role in harming working people. There is no organization better positioned to help elect Democrats up and down the ballot, from local office to the Oval Office. Vice President Kamala Devi Harris was born in Oakland, California, on October 20, 1964. Harris is the daughter of immigrants. Her father is a Jamaican economics professor and her mother was a scientist working on breast cancer, who came to the United States from India at the age of 19 and then received her doctorate the same year that Kamala was born. clean_body: | | | Hi Friend, Welcome to the latest New Pennsylvania Project newsletter! In this edition, you'll find critical election news, upcoming events, and exciting career opportunities. We’re here to keep you informed about our progress to eliminate voting barriers. We will continue to provide key election updates, and highlight the issues that shape Pennsylvania's future. As we gear up for the 2024 general election, we invite you to join us in our mission to mobilize voters to the polls in every election, and to make change in our communities. #WhenWeVoteWeWin | | | | | | | | GETTY Vice President Kamala Devi Harris was born in Oakland, California, on October 20, 1964. Harris is the daughter of immigrants. Her father is a Jamaican economics professor and her mother was a scientist working on breast cancer, who came to the United States from India at the age of 19 and then received her doctorate the same year that Kamala was born. Her whole career path from law to politics has been defined by many firsts. She was the first Indian American senator and California’s first female and South Asian attorney general. Speaking of her mother ten years after her passing, Harris said: "My mother would look at me and she’d say, ‘Kamala, you may be the first to do many things, but make sure you are not the last.'"- On January 20, 2021, Kamala Harris was sworn in as Vice President of the United States – the first woman, the first Black American, and the first South Asian American to be elected to this position. Now, as to position her as the Democratic Party’s 2024 presidential nominee, Harris could be on the cusp of becoming the country’s first female president. "Now that President Joe Biden has dropped out of the presidential race and endorsed Harris, it seems likely she will be the new nominee. Here’s her record on voting rights in the Biden administration and in her career as a senator." “For the first time in at least 16 years, the Democratic and Republican parties in Pennsylvania are within half a million registered voters of one another...The number of people registered as independents or under a third party has also grown, from 11% of total registered voters in 2008 to 15% this year.” "A flurry of recent bipartisan agreements by state lawmakers on energy projects and policies is sending a clear message: Pennsylvania is slowly moving toward clean energy but fossil fuels aren’t going anywhere." “Whether Gov. Josh Shapiro wins the veepstakes or not, Democratic lawmakers and officials expressed confidence that Pennsylvania will deliver a victory in the Nov. 5 presidential election for their party’s standard bearer Kamala Harris.” “If Shapiro is chosen as Kamala Harris' running mate and they win the presidential election, Davis would take over as Pennsylvania's governor...Davis is prepared to take over whenever he may be asked, he said at a news conference Wednesday in Lancaster.” “As Ms. Harris turns her attention to selecting a running mate, the interviews show no clear consensus among this group of party insiders over whom she should pick: 16 percent of respondents said it should be Josh Shapiro, the governor of Pennsylvania, and 11 percent said Mark Kelly, the senator from Arizona. About 28 percent of respondents said they did not know whom the selection should be, or they did not respond to the question.” “The campaign said earlier it took in $81 million in the 24 hours after Mr. Biden dropped out. It was the largest amount of money raised in a 24-hour span in presidential history, according to Team Harris...The $100 million haul came from more than 1.1 million unique donors, including 62% first-time donors.” “In Pennsylvania, should the Democrats retain the White House in November and Shapiro moves onto Washington, Lt. Gov. Austin Davis would assume the governor’s role, while Senate President Pro Tempore Kim Ward (R-Westmoreland) will take over as Lieutenant Governor and become President of the Senate.” "Pennsylvania’s highest court will weigh in on the legality of Pittsburgh’s tax on out-of-town athletes and performers. In an order issued Monday, the state Supreme Court said it would hear arguments about whether lower courts misinterpreted a constitutional requirement that taxes be levied uniformly." . | | | Breaking barriers: Pennsylvanians share why Kamala Harris’ presidential bid gives them hope “Besides the representation part, which is important, in my case... my daughter was conceived by IVF and so basically it concerns me that this choice could be taken away or even eliminated.” -Dyneco Gibson Read in how New Pennsylvania Project's board members, Senator Patty Kim, and Speaker of the House, Joanna McClinton, along with NPP's director of campaigns & engagement, Dyneco Gibson, and our CEO, Kadida Kenner, are finding inspiration in Vice President Kamala Harris’ run for the White House. CEO Kadida Kenner as guest speaker on Areva Martin in Real Time "We are experiencing a climate in which women of all races, all creeds, are standing up for themselves and what is best for them." Watch Kadida Kenner talk about what is at stake during this election during her interview with Areva Martin on KBLA 1580. | | | | | | | | | UNITED AGAINST PROJECT 2025 / AGENDA 47 RALLY Saturday, July 27th, 2024 at 6:30 pmChester County Historic Courthouse 3 N High St, West Chester, PA 19380 New Pennsylvania Project's CEO, Kadida Kenner, will be there to help open up the event. We need to do everything in our power to keep Project 2025 and now Agenda 47 from happening. | Join us in the City of Chester for a Block Party to celebrate our Headquarters Grand Opening! The New Pennsylvania Project has a new headquarters in the City of Chester. Save the date for the celebration on Tuesday, August 13th, from 5:30-8:00 pm at 2619 9th Street, Chester, PA. This is a family-friendly event with FREE food, sweet treats, activities for the kids, and of course, the opportunity to get registered to vote or check your voter's status. We will also have a screening of the documentary: "Suppressed and Sabotaged." For more information email us at: info@newpaproject.org | | | | | NPP ON THE GROUND New Philly regional organizing director, Marcus, engaging a voter at her door. | Connie talks to a man on his way to the bus. Fellow American,

I'm Tim Sheehy. Those are also my pronouns. _**SHEE – He.**_

**That's a joke** , but it shows the lunacy we're living with in Joe Biden and Jon Tester's America.

I'm a former Navy SEAL. My wife is a Marine. I led Americans in the battle to defend our country. Then, we came home to live the American Dream in Montana.

We started an aerial firefighting business in our barn. We created hundreds of jobs and protected our public lands and Montanans from devastating wildfires.

Here are just a few of the reasons that members like you gave for why you overwhelmingly voted to endorse Kamala Harris for President:
> _“Harris has worked to improve maternal health, she has met with dozens of foreign leaders, she has led the charge on reproductive rights. The Biden-Harris administration has helped so many of my friends by forgiving student loans, reducing the cost of insulin, and continuing the expansion of the child tax credit.” - Pamela C. from Alpharetta, GA_
> _“If we are to beat the Project 2025 agenda, VP Harris is our best shot. I am excited about voting in November for the first time in many years and think we should endorse her.” - Althea A. from Albuquerque, NM_
> _“We must protect the most vulnerable among us! That means blocking the fascist agenda and Donald Trump. It's as simple as that and right now Kamala Harris is the only functional vehicle that we have to blunt fascism, Project 2025, and the MAGA movement.” - Seth A. from Philadelphia, PA_
> _“As a black woman, she fights for causes that I care deeply about and am impacted by the most.” - Tyneisha H. from San Francisco, CA_
> _“When we choose between two futures, I want the one where the most pro-abortion access president in history has access to power, instead of the person who would deport immigrant communities, attack Black people, other people of color, and the working class, and take away even more rights from trans and LGBTQ+ people.” - Madeleine D. from New York, NY_
> _“Vice President Harris is the country's best chance to defeat Trump. I have serious concerns about Harris, and sincerely hope she will advocate for more progressive policies and a ceasefire in Gaza‚ but despite those concerns she has my vote.” - Dan C. from Houston, TX_
> _“Kamala es una mujer preparada y sera una buena contrincante para el criminal de Trump.” - Merline G. from Las Cruces, NM_
> _“Working people need an administration where we can organize and build power. While not perfect, a Harris administration would give us the conditions where we could win on many levels. We do not want Trump's people in charge of addressing the tax act that is expiring in 2025.” - Jasmine B. from Washington, DC_
> _“Kamala has been an ally and an advocate. She has acknowledged when her choices have been fumbled, but pushes forward to find a better way. I do believe Kamala will listen to those around her and continue striding forward towards a future I believe in.” - Audrea C. from Jeffersonville, IN_
> _“With nearly all potential challengers declining to run and endorsing Kamala Harris, it is time to get behind her. The last two days have been an amazing display of energy and enthusiasm, and WFP can help to keep this going with an endorsement.” - Chris R. from Wauwatosa, WI_

clean_body: Here are just a few of the reasons that members like you gave for why you overwhelmingly voted to endorse Kamala Harris for President | | | Peter — In case you missed the news this morning: The Working Families Party is endorsing Vice President Kamala Harris for president! Scroll down to read some of the reasons WFP members like you gave for why you wanted to get started right away on building the biggest possible movement to defeat Donald Trump in November. Earlier this week, we asked WFP members to share some of your thinking behind your votes in our endorsement process. Here are just a few of the reasons that members like you gave for why you overwhelmingly voted to endorse Kamala Harris for President: “Harris has worked to improve maternal health, she has met with dozens of foreign leaders, she has led the charge on reproductive rights. The Biden-Harris administration has helped so many of my friends by forgiving student loans, reducing the cost of insulin, and continuing the expansion of the child tax credit.” - Pamela C. from Alpharetta, GA “If we are to beat the Project 2025 agenda, VP Harris is our best shot. I am excited about voting in November for the first time in many years and think we should endorse her.” - Althea A. from Albuquerque, NM “We must protect the most vulnerable among us! That means blocking the fascist agenda and Donald Trump. It's as simple as that and right now Kamala Harris is the only functional vehicle that we have to blunt fascism, Project 2025, and the MAGA movement.” - Seth A. from Philadelphia, PA “As a black woman, she fights for causes that I care deeply about and am impacted by the most.” - Tyneisha H. from San Francisco, CA “When we choose between two futures, I want the one where the most pro-abortion access president in history has access to power, instead of the person who would deport immigrant communities, attack Black people, other people of color, and the working class, and take away even more rights from trans and LGBTQ+ people.” - Madeleine D. from New York, NY “Vice President Harris is the country's best chance to defeat Trump. I have serious concerns about Harris, and sincerely hope she will advocate for more progressive policies and a ceasefire in Gaza‚ but despite those concerns she has my vote.” - Dan C. from Houston, TX “Kamala es una mujer preparada y sera una buena contrincante para el criminal de Trump.” - Merline G. from Las Cruces, NM “Working people need an administration where we can organize and build power. While not perfect, a Harris administration would give us the conditions where we could win on many levels. We do not want Trump's people in charge of addressing the tax act that is expiring in 2025.” - Jasmine B. from Washington, DC “Kamala has been an ally and an advocate. She has acknowledged when her choices have been fumbled, but pushes forward to find a better way. I do believe Kamala will listen to those around her and continue striding forward towards a future I believe in.” - Audrea C. from Jeffersonville, IN “With nearly all potential challengers declining to run and endorsing Kamala Harris, it is time to get behind her. The last two days have been an amazing display of energy and enthusiasm, and WFP can help to keep this going with an endorsement.” - Chris R. from Wauwatosa, WI WFP members may differ on the reasons for their votes, but one thing we’re all clear on is this: we know that if we are going to build a government responsive to working people, we’ll first need to join together to defeat Trump and MAGA this fall. And to do that, we’ll have to build a massive voter outreach program to knock on doors, hit the phones, get on the airwaves, and turn out voters across the country. We did it in 2020, and we can do it again. But we can’t do it without you. Are you with us? Onward, Working Families Party P.S. Thoughts? Feedback? We want to hear it. subject: Leveling with you
disclaimer_text: Paid For By Gallego for Arizona
body:
We know what it takes to win tough elections in Arizona. Grit, determination, discipline — but also, a staggering amount of money. And like I said at the start of this email... over the last few weeks it’s begun to look like we’re not raising the kind of resources that can do it.
#

I’ve got to level with you right now, Peter.
I don’t know if we’re raising what we need to win in Arizona.
The entire race has changed over the last month. The last three weeks have been a major turning point for our nation, and the stakes have never been higher — or clearer — in Arizona.
In 2020, Arizona was the difference between winning back the White House and four more years of Trump, and Arizona’s seat cemented our Senate majority. In 2022, Arizona was the state that preserved our Senate majority.
And in 2024, whether we win or lose is going to play the defining role in whether or not we maintain control in the Senate, and whether we defeat Trump once and for all.
We know what it takes to win tough elections in Arizona. Grit, determination, discipline — but also, a staggering amount of money. And like I said at the start of this email... over the last few weeks it’s begun to look like we’re not raising the kind of resources that can do it.
Kari Lake and the MAGA-right are on the move out here. Our only chance at stopping them is to hit our fundraising goals. These aren’t just arbitrary numbers — they’re what we need to hit to win.

body:
The last few days have been a real rush.
|
---
| | There's one word I can think of to sum up the last few days for the Democratic Party: **energy.** There is _energy_ in our party as people rally behind Kamala Harris. _Energy_ as we see her make the case against Trump and offer a powerful alternative vision for the future. **_Energy_****as we mobilize to win this election in just over 100 days.** I'm proud to do my small part to keep that energy going as I work to help Kamala make history and bolster Democrats in key Senate races, so that she has a majority in January that's ready to pass the agenda Americans need. We're hoping to get 100 donations by the end of this week. [**Can you split $3 now between me and Kamala Harris?**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/89575286/487737989/-118994385?refcode=2024-07-25-harris&recurring=&amount=3&amounts=10,30,50,100,200&refcode2=5f96dcb1-dd4a-ef11-86c3-6045bdd9e096&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNDEvMS84OTQxMiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI1Zjk2ZGNiMS1kZDRhLWVmMTEtODZjMy02MDQ1YmRkOWUwOTYiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=PJFNzZnxXvhrGQjV_opfBpz5sGj_jUhnZ-PAJWa7rZQ=) I'm fired up, and I hope you are too. _Ron_ Forwarded Message | [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/89575287/487737990/2140832878?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNDEvMS84OTQxMiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI1Zjk2ZGNiMS1kZDRhLWVmMTEtODZjMy02MDQ1YmRkOWUwOTYiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=PJFNzZnxXvhrGQjV_opfBpz5sGj_jUhnZ-PAJWa7rZQ=&emci=867acd79-c24a-ef11-86c3-6045bdd9e096&emdi=5f96dcb1-dd4a-ef11-86c3-6045bdd9e096&ceid=9818364)

By now I'm sure you've seen the news that President Joe Biden has made the decision to withdraw his candidacy for President of the United States.
I've been proud to work with President Biden on a record number of Democratic successes these past three-and-a-half years. From the bipartisan infrastructure bill to the CHIPS Act to the historic Inflation Reduction Act, under President Biden's leadership, Democrats have gained enormous ground in the fight to hold Big Pharma accountable and set us on course to a clean energy future.
We've also made major gains in the fights against wealthy tax cheats, and in tackling the climate crisis head-on. I have no doubt that history will judge well those landmark achievements.

name: Sarah McBride
subject: What we're about to start spending $ on
body:
We have to start making decisions about what we can spend our funds on — and what we can't.
#
"What are we going to spend on TV and digital ads?"
"Can we afford to do 4, 5, or 6 pieces of mail?"
"How many more organizers can we hire to knock on doors and call voters?"
These are the questions I'm discussing with my campaign leadership team _right now_. **With less than 7 weeks until our primary and just over 100 days until the General Election, we have to start making decisions about what we can spend our funds on — and what we can't.**
We've agreed that to pull off the basics, we need to raise another $10,000 in online grassroots contributions before July is over. To run a campaign we are confident we can win, we need to raise $20,000.
I've always been an overachiever. 😊 So I REALLY want to hit that ideal goal before July is over. [**Can you help by donating $5 or anything you can spare right now? If just 1% of people reading this email pitch in just a little bit, we’ll reach it!**](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/mcb-em-20240725-1?refcode=em20240725-1-880&amount=5&refcode2=880_21716__e4ofL&akid=880%2E21716%2E_e4ofL)
[****](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/mcb-em-20240725-1?refcode=em20240725-1&refcode2=880_21716__e4ofL&akid=880%2E21716%2E_e4ofL)
You might think because Delaware is small, our budget would be too. But running for Congress isn’t cheap.

body:
Part of the story starts one morning in the 1970s.

| | | [ ](https://act.elizabethwarren.com/go/216?t=3&akid=2286%2E4032634%2E22Y_Km)
---
**This week marks the 13th anniversary of when the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau (CFPB) opened for business** — one year after President Obama signed Wall Street reform into law. I had worked hard to create this agency that has the sole purpose of looking out for consumers — because I’d dedicated my career to studying why families go broke and pushing to rebuild the middle class. And part of the story starts one morning in the 1970s, when I forgot about a few pieces of bread I’d left in the toaster oven — and nearly set my kitchen on fire. Back then, our toaster oven had an on-off switch, and that was it. At some point, someone had the bright idea of adding a timer and automatic shut-off. This simple change made it a whole lot harder for distracted mothers, or anyone else, to leave it running until it set the kitchen on fire. Thirty years later, while working on an article about how the government could protect consumers from predatory financial companies, I thought about those old toaster ovens: If government agencies can monitor toasters for basic safety, keep lead paint out of children’s toys, and keep rat poison out of medicine, why couldn’t the government have an agency that looked out for consumers using financial products? It was possible to refinance a home with a mortgage that had a one-in-five chance of costing a family their home and putting them out on the street. In fact, it wasn’t just possible: Those mortgages were bursting into flames all over the country. I had a plan for how we could change the rules with a structural fix: A new government agency that could make sure financial companies followed some clear, commonsense rules. No tricks hidden in the fine print, no traps buried in complex legalese. People said the idea was pie-in-the-sky. But that didn’t stop labor unions, and civil rights organizations, and consumer groups, and so many others from jumping into the fight. And you know it didn’t stop me. **We organized. Fought hard. And won.** And since then, the CFPB has:
* Put over $20 billion back in the hands of people who got cheated by financial institutions
* Imposed over $4.8 billion in penalties on lawbreakers
* Eliminated at least one medical collection from 22.8 million people’s credit reports
* Secured $183 million in monetary relief for actions harming service members and veterans
* And much more

But make no mistake: the CFPB’s opponents are staying on the attack. They’ve tried bogus lawsuit after bogus lawsuit, they’ve tried every trick in the book to block this agency — because after all, it has held them accountable. It has put over $20 billion back in the pockets of seniors, students, service members, veterans, families struggling to make it to the end of the month, and other consumers who got cheated by financial institutions. So as we think about the work ahead to defend the CFPB, we remember the big victory that created it in the first place. We did what some people thought would be impossible. **We must use that same grit and grassroots organizing to keep the CFPB thriving, and to stay in the fight for universal child care, reproductive freedom, taxing the ultra-rich, and so much more.** [**That’s how we win. Will you add your name today to support the CFPB and say you support it for all the years to come?**](https://act.elizabethwarren.com/signup/ew-em-cfpb/?source=EMZ21U_FTC_E_20240725_V1S1&t=8&akid=2286%2E4032634%2E22Y_Km) | [**ADD MY NAME**](https://act.elizabethwarren.com/signup/ew-em-cfpb/?source=EMZ21U_FTC_E_20240725_V1S1&t=9&akid=2286%2E4032634%2E22Y_Km)
---
Thanks for being a part of this,
Elizabeth

I had a plan for how we could change the rules with a structural fix: A new government agency that could make sure financial companies followed some clear, commonsense rules. No tricks hidden in the fine print, no traps buried in complex legalese. People said the idea was pie-in-the-sky. But that didn’t stop labor unions, and civil rights organizations, and consumer groups, and so many others from jumping into the fight. And you know it didn’t stop me. We organized. Fought hard. And won. And since then, the CFPB has: Put over $20 billion back in the hands of people who got cheated by financial institutions Imposed over $4.8 billion in penalties on lawbreakers Eliminated at least one medical collection from 22.8 million people’s credit reports Secured $183 million in monetary relief for actions harming service members and veterans And much more But make no mistake: the CFPB’s opponents are staying on the attack. They’ve tried bogus lawsuit after bogus lawsuit, they’ve tried every trick in the book to block this agency — because after all, it has held them accountable. It has put over $20 billion back in the pockets of seniors, students, service members, veterans, families struggling to make it to the end of the month, and other consumers who got cheated by financial institutions. So as we think about the work ahead to defend the CFPB, we remember the big victory that created it in the first place. We did what some people thought would be impossible. We must use that same grit and grassroots organizing to keep the CFPB thriving, and to stay in the fight for universal child care, reproductive freedom, taxing the ultra-rich, and so much more.** | Thanks for being a part of this, Elizabeth | | | | | | | | | ---|---|---|--- | Paid for by Warren for Senate All content © 2024 Warren for Senate, All Rights Reserved PO Box 171375, Boston, MA 02117 | | This email was sent to dpwillis67@gmail.com We'll miss you, but you can always .
